per_pair.why: Game B's compass is far more visually polished with clear gradient shading and strong silhouette; Game A's hearts are readable but plain.
Game B's integrated health display and compass show better feedback and visual finish; Game A's large text overlay feels intrusive compared to B's cohesive UI.

loser_biggest_gap: Integrate UI elements as meaningful parts of the game world rather than flat overlays; add gradient shading, visual depth, and art direction that makes every HUD element feel crafted and intentional.
loser_other_gaps: Replace the cramped item/icon bar with larger, clearer icons that can be parsed instantly during gameplay
Remove debug-style text overlays (like 'ARENA 1/5' and 'SEED 99') that break immersion and visual polish
Establish a cohesive visual language where all UI elements (hearts, items, text) use consistent styling and shading
reasoning: Game B demonstrates superior polish through integrated UI design, gradient shading, and visual cohesion with the game world. While Game A is cleaner and slightly more readable, it lacks the craft and visual personality of a highly-rated indie game. Game B's compass and health displays show significantly more care in execution. Game A's utilitarian approach sacrifices the visual appeal that makes players feel the game is polished and finished.
